origin: T33 hand-off (Ian team research, 2026-10-24); re-verified by T38

source.title: Development of high sustained anti-drug antibody titers and corresponding clinical decline in a late-onset Pompe disease patient after 11+ years on enzyme replacement therapy.
source.patient: Single patient (followed from infancy to about 15 years)

diagnosis.name: glycogen storage disease II (late-onset Pompe disease)

confirmation.summary: Muscle biopsy, enzyme analysis and GAA sequencing (c.525delT and c.-32-13T>G) at 9 months.
evidence: The diagnosis of Pompe disease was confirmed at age 9 months by muscle biopsy, enzyme analysis, and GAA sequence analysis
compound heterozygosity for c.525delT and c.-32-13T >G, predictive of LOPD

note.text: My child was slow to learn to move and walk, and the muscles seemed weak even as a toddler. When walking began, the feet were set far apart and the lower back curved more than expected. Walking and climbing stairs kept taking extra effort as the years went on. Around age twelve, a sideways curve in the back became bad enough to need surgery. By the teenage years, balance was worse, falls were happening and there was less energy for walking.
note.author: T33 hand-off (assistant-written from the article; not the parent's words)
